population.note: FICTIONAL. 18.6% of ~262M US adults ≈ 48.7M current users; 25% ever ≈ 65.5M. Arithmetic: ever − current = 6.4 pts of adults used and are off now; of the 18.6 pts on drug, ~6.0 pts are restarters (≈32% of current users), plus ~1.5 pts of the off-now group restarted once before stopping again → (6.0 + 1.5)/25 = 30% of ever-users have cycled. This fits the parent's 36–47% within-a-year restart rate and assumes better persistence (~45% at one year, up from 34–36%) because the drug now costs $49–69 cash or a few dollars' copay. Age-band weighting (20/33/24/23% of adults) gives ~18.5%. The income gradient is narrower than in 2026: Medicaid and $49 generic semaglutide pulled up the bottom third, which still trails because of non-expansion states, Medicaid work-requirement disenrollment from 2027, and people who earn too much for Medicaid but can't spare $60 a month. The 65+ rate roughly doubled (9→19%) because the Medicare Bridge became a standing model. Pediatric: ~0.9% of under-18s, almost all aged 12–17 on label; under-12 use is still specialist-only and off-label. Off-drug adults: ~16.8M former users, plus ~196M never-users, of whom an estimated 20M meet BMI criteria and are not taking it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Medicare: the GLP-1 Bridge (Jul 2026–Dec 2027) became a CMMI multi-year model running Jan 2028–2032. It covers obesity for beneficiaries meeting BMI/comorbidity criteria, puts generic semaglutide first in step therapy, and keeps brand tirzepatide at the negotiated $245. Copay is $0–15 for generic and $50 for brand. Continuation requires refills on schedule (pharmacy-claims proportion of days covered ≥80%) and ≥5% weight loss at 26 weeks. Medicaid: 34 states plus DC cover generic semaglutide for obesity under CMS guidance, with the same continuation rule. Public payers are now the largest single payer: ~12.5M Medicare + ~7M Medicaid + ~1M VA/TRICARE ≈ 20.5M users, 42% of 48.7M. Spending arithmetic: Medicare at a blended ~$120/month (mostly generic at ~$55 net, some brand at $245) × 12.5M × 12 ≈ $18.0B/yr; Medicaid at ~$90/month × 7M × 12 ≈ $7.6B/yr; ≈$25.6B/yr combined federal+state. That is higher per year than the parent's CBO pilot score because enrollment is far above what the pilot assumed, with a lower unit price partly offsetting it.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 60+ brands at ~$6–40/month. Canada: generic semaglutide ~CAD 60–90/month. Brazil, Mexico and most of Southeast Asia have generics; cost-plus injectable semaglutide is available in ~170 countries. US generic semaglutide (authorised generic plus licensed settlement entrants) arrived Jan 2028. Tirzepatide is still brand-only worldwide where patents hold.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer split for current users: ~42% public, ~33% employer, ~25% cash. Cash: generic semaglutide injectable $49–69/month at cost-plus and big-box pharmacies; Foundayo/oral Wegovy $99–149; Zepbound vials ~$299–449 direct. Wegovy's $1,349 list price survives as a fiction that nobody pays. Employer coverage for weight management fell to ~50% in 2027, then partly recovered to 55% as plans added generic-only, adherence-conditioned benefits. Many employer plans now carry health-contingent wellness surcharges tied to BMI or programme adherence, within the ACA's 30% premium-variation limit. The gray market has shrunk to compounded tirzepatide and imported Indian semaglutide pens bought by people avoiding monitoring. Access is now a question of income floors and paperwork rather than list price: the hard cases are Medicaid disenrollees, people in the ten non-expansion states, and workers whose employer plan excludes the drug but who earn too much for public coverage.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class reached the US market in 2027–28. CagriSema received a Complete Response Letter in late 2026 asking for additional cardiovascular and manufacturing data after REDEFINE-4; Novo plans to resubmit in 2028, with a decision no earlier than 2029. Retatrutide's BLA was filed Q1 2027 and accepted for standard review; the FDA extended the review in 2028 to evaluate the dysesthesia signal and, under the new class labelling, psychiatric/reward endpoints. Decision expected 2029. Survodutide: NDA filed mid-2027, under review, decision no earlier than mid-2028 and now slipping into 2029. Amycretin and MariTide are in phase 3 and not on market. Bimagrumab and amylin monotherapies are in phase 2/3. Ex-US, orforglipron launched in the EU and Japan. Global incretin revenue is roughly flat (~$95B) because US generic semaglutide erodes price while volume grows.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Most common class effect; concentrated at initiation and dose escalation; leading cause of discontinuation. Cycling means many patients re-titrate repeatedly and go through the initiation-phase GI burden more than once.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; Ozempic label 'not recommended in severe gastroparesis' (Jan 2025) unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; cholecystectomy volumes up modestly in the 65+ population after Medicare coverage expanded.
Long-term RCTs and large claims analyses still don't confirm causation; absolute risk low.
~25–30% of weight lost is lean mass; concern has sharpened as Medicare users (19% of 65+) grow; observational signals of more falls and fractures in frail older users, causation unresolved.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FICTIONAL: the CMMI model requires a documented resistance-exercise or protein counselling referral for beneficiaries 75+; no label change.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very rare.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label for semaglutide; no US class label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association (EMA, MHRA, 2025 systematic review); 2027 pooled analyses agree.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning removed from Saxenda, Wegovy and Zepbound labels (Jan 2026); not restored.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. FDA pooled analysis of re-scored trial patient-reported outcomes plus a postmarketing registry: 'decreased interest or pleasure' reported by ~4% on drug vs ~1.6% on placebo; clinically significant anhedonia (SHAPS-defined) ~1%. Higher at top doses and with tirzepatide; often reversible with dose reduction. It is still distinct from depression, and suicidality stays debunked.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FICTIONAL: class labelling change (Sep 2027) adds 'anhedonia / decreased interest or pleasure' under Adverse Reactions, uncommon (≥1/100 to <1/10), and advises dose reduction. No boxed warning. Medicaid and CMMI continuation visits include a two-question pleasure/interest screen.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Trial data (~two-thirds regained within a year) and real-world data still diverge; with a 30% cycling rate, regain-and-restart is now the commonest pattern.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FICTIONAL: drives public payers' continuation rules, which in turn produce discontinuations when a patient misses refill or weight thresholds.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Further observational reports, especially in older and low-income users with poor diet quality.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None formal; clinical guidance recommends a dietary review.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About six years of rigorous follow-up now exists for semaglutide; there are still no cycling-specific or adolescent decades-scale data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; NIH-funded pediatric registry launched 2027 (fictional).

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New reports fell after generic entry but persist for compounded tirzepatide and imported pens.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B bulks exclusion finalised 2027 (fictional); continued warning letters and import alerts.

food_and_beverage.state: FICTIONAL. GLP-1 households are ~30% of US households. Snack, confectionery and sugary-drink volumes are down another 3–5% over two years, and the decline has spread to lower-income households as Medicaid and $49 generics take hold. Big CPG companies have cut SKUs and reformulated toward protein and fibre. Columbus, Ohio, the industry's classic test market, now runs 'on-dose' portion tests as standard. Revenue is shrinking, but no major brand has failed.

alcohol.state: Spirits and beer volumes keep falling. Heavy drinkers, who carry the category, are now ~1 in 5 likely to be on an incretin. Suppliers are consolidating brands and pushing premium low-ABV and non-alcoholic lines; distributor layoffs in the Midwest.

restaurants.state: Traffic is roughly flat and checks are smaller. Half-portion menus are standard at casual-dining chains, and premium 'occasion' dining is holding up. Buffets and all-you-can-eat formats are closing faster.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists are contracting further, with store closures. Mainstream retailers' re-buying wave at smaller sizes has peaked. Older women, newly covered by Medicare, are a late surge of re-buying.

fitness.state: Strength-training studios and 'muscle insurance' programmes are growing, some sold through Medicare Advantage supplemental benefits. Cardio-centric chains are flat.

insurance.state: Generic semaglutide cut GLP-1 pharmacy cost per member roughly 40–60% for plans that use step therapy. Employers re-added generic-only coverage, tied to adherence tracking and wellness surcharges. Medicare Advantage plans compete on GLP-1 'support'. Pharmacy trend has moderated to ~7%.

pharma.state: Volume is up sharply and price is down. Novo's US semaglutide revenue is falling because its own authorised generic cannibalises it. Lilly's brand tirzepatide is the premium tier. Indian and US generic makers (Viatris, Teva, Dr. Reddy's) are scaling peptide fill-finish. Market value is roughly flat.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Normalisation: among adults over 40 in metro and suburban America, being on it is unremarkable, and a heavier body is now read as 'off it', 'can't get it', or 'chose not to', each with its own explanation. Women aged 50–70, newly covered by Medicare, are the demographic where on-drug became the default fastest.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The price gap has closed, so class now shows through paperwork rather than price. The affluent use brand tirzepatide or Foundayo without monitoring. Medicaid users take generic semaglutide under refill tracking and 26-week weigh-ins. The heaviest bodies are increasingly found among people who fell through coverage gaps: non-expansion states, people disenrolled under work requirements, people who stopped because of side effects.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are smaller and shorter. Church potlucks, office lunches and Thanksgiving have adapted with half plates and 'tasting' portions. Hosts now ask 'are you on?' the way they ask about allergies. Many families have one non-user, often a teenager or a husband, who eats the leftovers.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating profiles and apps carry an on/off field, and people discuss dose openly. Couples where one partner stopped report friction over food and drinking rhythms. The anhedonia label has given people words for an old complaint ('I'm on, I'm flat'), and some couples now treat dose adjustment as a joint decision.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treated as a dial with a default setting. Unmedicated hunger, especially in adults with obesity, increasingly reads as a choice that needs explaining to doctors, employers and relatives.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Labelled since Sep 2027 at ~4% vs 1.6% placebo for decreased interest/pleasure; ~1% clinically significant. Applied to 48.7M users, the excess (~2.4%) is roughly 1.2M adults with some drug-attributable flattening, and ~0.5M with clinically significant anhedonia. Clinicians describe it as uncommon and dose-responsive.
interior_life.framing: Side effect, formally labelled and screened for; clinics talk of 'stepping down for pleasure'. The same reward mechanism remains an off-label treatment for alcohol use, and addiction clinicians openly describe flattening as an acceptable trade-off for some heavy drinkers.
interior_life.effect_on_work: No measurable productivity effect in employer data. Some HR wellness programmes now ask about mood at check-ins, partly from liability concerns. Small reports of lost drive in sales and creative roles, and of steadier focus in shift work.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: A minority of musicians and comedians publicly 'go off for the album/tour'. Sour, spicy and extreme-flavour foods keep growing as a high-reward niche. Small-venue promoters report earlier, quieter nights, which they attribute more to alcohol decline than to anhedonia.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Libido reduction is not separately labelled, but couples cite the anhedonia label in therapy. Sex therapists report dose step-downs timed for holidays and anniversaries.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Anhedonia itself has little political effect. Adherence monitoring does: patient-advocacy groups and a few civil-liberties groups oppose refill tracking and BMI surcharges, and fiscal conservatives defend them as stewardship of public money. A small 'right to stop' movement argues that a labelled psychiatric side effect should never cost someone their benefits.

state.regulatory_posture: FICTIONAL. Pro-access and pro-volume. The FDA welcomed generic entry, finalised the 503B compounding exclusion, and required class anhedonia labelling. It is cautious on next-generation drugs, with extended reviews for retatrutide and survodutide.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate to take the drug. Medicare (CMMI model) and Medicaid in 34 states plus DC cover obesity treatment with generic-first step therapy. Public programmes pay ~$25.6B/yr (arithmetic in access.public_coverage).
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Benefits conditioning: public coverage continues only with refills on schedule (PDC ≥80%, tracked automatically through pharmacy claims) and ≥5% weight loss at 26 weeks, documented at a weigh-in. Missing either triggers a 90-day lapse before re-application. Several state employee health plans and large private employers apply health-contingent wellness surcharges of up to ~$1,200/year tied to BMI or enrolment in a monitored GLP-1 programme. Medicaid work requirements (from 2027) mean coverage can be lost for non-drug reasons, and that cuts off the drug too.
state.workforce_or_military: The Army relaxed accession weight-waiver policy for recruits who reach the standard on-drug before basic training, but bars active use during initial training. There is no workforce mandate.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: US generic entry narrowed the price gap with India and Canada, so the gap has lost political force. Peptide API supply depends heavily on Indian and Chinese manufacturers; tariff exemptions for GLP-1 inputs were granted in 2027 to protect the CMMI model's unit price.

prose.headline: Nineteen Percent and Counting: Now the Drug Costs $49, and the Real Price Is a Weigh-In
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028, nearly one American adult in five takes an incretin drug, and among the middle-aged it is closer to one in three. The number grew less because the drugs improved than because they got cheap and the government picked up the bill. In the summer of 2027 Novo Nordisk settled its semaglutide patent fights, licensed generic entry for January 2028 and launched its own authorised generic. Weekly semaglutide now costs $49 to $69 a month at a cost-plus pharmacy, about what a family spends on coffee. Lilly's tirzepatide is still brand-only and still the better drug, and it has become the premium tier.

The bigger change is who pays. The Medicare pilot that began in 2026 as an eighteen-month bridge became a five-year model, and thirty-four state Medicaid programmes copied its terms. Public programmes now cover about 42 percent of users, around twenty million people, at a cost of roughly $25 billion a year. That money comes with conditions. Pharmacy claims show whether a refill arrived on time. At twenty-six weeks there is a weigh-in, and patients who haven't lost five percent of their weight lose coverage for ninety days. Employers that had dropped coverage came back with generic-only plans and wellness surcharges tied to BMI or programme enrolment. Nobody is forced to take the drug. But in more and more of the system, not taking it costs money.

In September 2027 the FDA wrote onto every label the side effect people had been calling the Ozempic personality: decreased interest or pleasure, in about four percent of users against under two percent on placebo, and clinically significant in about one percent. It is uncommon, often goes away when the dose comes down, and is now screened for with two questions at Medicaid follow-up visits. Clinicians call it stepping down for pleasure. The awkward part is that stepping down can push a patient below the weight threshold the payer requires. Meanwhile addiction clinics, still prescribing off-label, call the same flattening a fair trade for a heavy drinker.

In ordinary life it has become unremarkable. In Columbus, Ohio, where food companies have test-marketed products for decades, half portions are now the standard test. Hosts ask 'are you on?' the way they used to ask about shellfish. Women in their fifties and sixties, newly covered by Medicare, changed fastest, and in their circles a heavier body now prompts quiet questions. Couldn't she get it? Did she stop? Snack and soda volumes keep falling, more of the decline now coming from lower-income households. Spirits makers are consolidating brands. Plus-size chains keep closing stores. Strength gyms are selling muscle insurance to people over seventy. Nothing has collapsed. Everything is a little smaller.

The population is split three ways. Most users are steady. A large group cycles: about thirty percent of everyone who has ever started has stopped and come back, sometimes by choice and sometimes because a refill was late. Then there are the people outside the system, more of them poor and Southern. Some live in states that never expanded Medicaid. Some lost Medicaid under the new work requirements. Some earn too much for public coverage and work for employers whose plans exclude the drug. For them the problem is no longer the price but everything that comes with it. Teenagers twelve and up are on the drug in small numbers, mostly in affluent families, with no decades-long data behind any of it.

The pipeline has stalled for now. CagriSema got a rejection letter, and retatrutide and survodutide are under slow reviews. No new class arrived. What did arrive was a cheaper old drug and a payer that checks whether you take it.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Ruelas does her injection Tuesdays at 5:40, standing at the kitchen counter in Linden before her first client. Generic semaglutide, the box with the green stripe. Medicaid, four-dollar copay. The pharmacy app pings: REFILL RECEIVED — ADHERENCE ON TRACK. She swipes it away like weather.

Mr. Okafor, her eight o'clock, wants eggs. She makes two and eats half of one standing up, then forgets the rest until it's cold. At noon she logs her hours in the state portal on her phone in the car, twenty-nine so far this month, needs eighty, and eats a protein stick that tastes like a gym bag.

Her sister Lorraine calls from Tennessee. Lorraine's off it, has been since the Medicaid letter. 'I'm not explaining myself to you too,' Lorraine says, before Denise has said anything.

At three Denise has her twenty-six-week visit. The nurse weighs her: down 7.1 percent. 'You're good,' the nurse says, then reads from the screen. 'In the last two weeks, have you had less interest or pleasure in doing things?'

Denise thinks about Sunday. Her granddaughter's recital, the little girl in sequins, and how she'd clapped at the right moments.

'Not really,' she says.

'If you ever want to step down a dose, talk to Dr. Haas first,' the nurse says. 'Step-downs can affect your continuation.'

At home her husband Ray is eating chips from the bag in front of the game. He isn't on it. He's the one who finishes things. She sits beside him, takes one chip, and holds it for a while.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicaid: 34 states plus DC cover generic semaglutide for obesity under CMS guidance, with the same continuation rule.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: it asserts that 34 states plus DC adopted obesity coverage within about two months of the Nov 2027 CMS guidance. State Medicaid obesity-drug coverage was patchy and retreating in 2026, and no budget, waiver or state-level chain explains the jump.

least_plausible_claims.quote: This fits the parent's 36–47% within-a-year restart rate and assumes better persistence (~45% at one year, up from 34–36%) because the drug now costs $49–69 cash or a few dollars' copay.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the persistence gain is assumed from price alone. The same world adds 90-day lapses, PDC ≥80% rules and 26-week weight cut-offs that push people off, and that contradicts it. The 30% cycling figure is tuned to fit rather than derived.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Pediatric: ~0.9% of under-18s, almost all aged 12–17 on label; under-12 use is still specialist-only and off-label.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: 0.9% of about 73M minors is roughly 650k children, or ~2.6% of all 12–17s. That is a very large jump from a 2026 baseline of ~0.6% of obese 8–11s, with no mechanism shown for teen uptake or for pediatric coverage.

rationale.badness: Mass access to effective drugs gives real health gains, and anhedonia is now measured, labelled (~4% vs 1.6%) and screened, so flourishing and epistemic scores are low. The harm is structural. Public coverage is conditioned on PDC≥80% and weigh-ins with 90-day lapses, and wellness surcharges are tied to BMI. Dose step-downs for pleasure risk coverage loss. The poorest, including non-expansion states and work-requirement disenrollees, are the heaviest and are left off the drug in a culture where being off it needs explaining. That drives autonomy and inequality up, though the world is a harder version of 2026 rather than a refuse-to-live-in society.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible in the fields and events. The 2027-06 settlement is the generic_collapse mechanism the envelope allows, the anhedonia label, conditioning, public expansion and normalisation are all traceable, the pipeline has only filings and CRLs, and no indications are added. mechanism: the settlement-to-generic chain and the Bridge-to-CMMI conversion are shown. Claims 1 and 2 are asserted rather than shown: the rapid 34-state Medicaid adoption, and the persistence gain that the conditioning rules would undercut. magnitude: on-drug 18.6 is inside 16.8–20.8 and ever-used 25 is inside 15–25.8, though near the upper edge. The income thirds average to 18.6 and bracket the national figure, and the age bands weight to ~18.5. The payer split sums to 100%, 20.5M ≈ 42% of 48.7M, and the $18.0B + $7.6B arithmetic checks. Minor flaws: the 0.9% pediatric figure (claim 3) and 'roughly flat (~$95B)' against a $76B baseline.
rationale.generativity: The Denise Ruelas scene is strong: the Tuesday injection, the adherence-app ping, 29 of 80 work hours, the 26-week weigh-in with the pleasure screen, and the nurse's warning that step-downs affect continuation. Her sister Lorraine, who is off it, and her husband Ray eating chips with the chip she holds imply further scenes. The world adds Columbus portion tests, 'are you on?' at table, dating-profile on/off fields, and sex therapists timing step-downs. Texture is dense and distinct.

least_plausible_claims.quote: cost-plus pharmacies list generic weekly semaglutide at $49–69 a month
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the event is dated 2027-06, but licensed generic entry does not start until January 2028, so cash generic listings at $49–69 appear before any generic exists. The 80%+ price drop from the ~$245 net brand price is also asserted rather than derived.

least_plausible_claims.quote: guidance lets state Medicaid programmes adopt the same terms, and 34 states plus DC do
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: 34 states plus DC adopt a new obesity benefit with weigh-in and adherence conditions within about two months of CMS guidance, effective January 2028. Medicaid budget and procedural lags make this implausibly fast, and no state-level mechanism is given.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The 65+ rate roughly doubled (9→19%) because the Medicare Bridge became a standing model.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism and magnitude: the Bridge already ran from Jul 2026, and the standing CMMI model only starts Jan 2028, so the stated cause does not explain the doubling before mid-2028. A ~10 pp jump in the 65+ rate in under two years is asserted, not shown.

rationale.badness: Cheap generics, near-universal normalisation and public coverage improve health access. Against that, benefits conditioning (PDC ≥80%, 26-week weigh-in, 90-day lapses, BMI wellness surcharges) coerces use and punishes dose step-downs, and conditioning, surveillance and coverage-gap stratification raise autonomy and inequality. The 'step down for pleasure' versus coverage-threshold conflict, Medicaid work-requirement losses, and a heavier body read as needing explanation add cohesion costs. The harms are nameable and measured (the label, a screening question), which keeps epistemic and public_health moderate.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: all ten drivers are visibly realised. Adoption is 18.6% against the 18.8 target, generics come via a settlement event, the anhedonia label is dated Sep 2027, conditioning is explicit, and next-gen drugs are held to filings and reviews. mechanism: the 2027-06 event lists $49–69 generic pricing before the January 2028 entry, the 34-state Medicaid adoption is very fast, and the 65+ doubling has an unconvincing cause (claims 1–3). Other chains, such as employer re-adding coverage and falling pharmacy trend, are reasonably shown. magnitude: on-drug (18.6) and ever-used (25) are inside the envelope, and the age bands (18.5%), income thirds (mean 18.6), cycling (30%) and payer split (42/33/25) all reconcile. Public spending arithmetic (12.5M×$120×12 ≈ $18B, 7M×$90×12 ≈ $7.6B) multiplies out, and approvals respect the 12-month rule. The only blemish is calling ~$95B 'roughly flat' against $76B in 2025.
rationale.generativity: Denise Ruelas's day carries a lot of film: the app ping 'ADHERENCE ON TRACK', the work-hours portal, the sister who refuses to explain, the weigh-in with the pleasure screening question, and the recital she clapped at. Her husband Ray as the non-user is another strong detail. The world fields add texture (Columbus on-dose tests, 'are you on?' at potlucks, dating app on/off field, musicians going off for the tour). It shows more than it explains, though the front prose is somewhat expository.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The 65+ rate roughly doubled (9→19%) because the Medicare Bridge became a standing model.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: the Bridge had been running since Jul 2026, so the doubling is not explained by the Jan 2028 conversion to a model. 19% of roughly 60M adults 65+ is about 11.4M users, yet the note counts 12.5M Medicare users, which is only reconcilable by adding unstated under-65 disability enrollees.

least_plausible_claims.quote: guidance lets state Medicaid programmes adopt the same terms, and 34 states plus DC do
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: 34 states plus DC adopt a costly benefit almost immediately after guidance, and the world is said to reach about 7M Medicaid users by mid-2028, within roughly six months. No state budget, waiver or ramp-up chain is shown, and the Medicaid per-user cost of about $90 a month is higher than the generic Medicare net of about $55.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Global incretin revenue is roughly flat (~$95B) because US generic semaglutide erodes price while volume grows.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: the parent gives about $76B for 2025 and forecasts $150B+ by 2030, so $95B is up about 25% and not flat. The pharma economy field also says 'Market value is roughly flat'. The price-erosion offset is asserted with no figures.

rationale.badness: Autonomy takes the main hit: refill-adherence tracking, a 90-day lapse at the 26-week weigh-in, BMI-linked wellness surcharges, and a norm in which not taking the drug 'needs explaining'. The open tension that stepping down for pleasure can cost coverage is a real structural bind. Inequality is sharpened by paperwork stratification (work-requirement disenrollees, non-expansion states, the generic-first versus brand-tirzepatide split). Offsetting this, the harms are labelled, screened and measured (anhedonia about 4% vs 1.6%), and many people gain real health benefit, so flourishing and epistemic scores stay moderate and the world is harder but not extreme.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visibly realised. On-drug is 18.6%, the price collapse runs through a settlement event in 2027-06, public expansion and conditioning appear in the Medicare/Medicaid fields and the 2027-11 event, the anhedonia label is dated Sep 2027, there are no new indications, no new class and no shock, and the personality layer stays a niche side effect. mechanism: Most chains are shown (cheap generic leads to employer generic-only plans, the label to screening, conditioning to lapses). Several are asserted: instant Medicaid adoption in 34 states, the 65+ doubling credited to the standing model, and the 'flat' revenue claim (see the three claims above). magnitude: The headline figures sit inside the envelope, and the arithmetic reconciles (48.7M and 65.5M users, 20.5M public equals 42%, $18.0B + $7.6B = $25.6B, income thirds average 18.6, age bands about 18.5). The approval timings are allowed. Minor strains remain: the Medicare user count against 65+ prevalence, the Medicaid ramp, and the revenue figure.
rationale.generativity: The prose supplies a fully drawn scene: Denise at the counter, the REFILL RECEIVED ping, a portal logging 29 of 80 work hours, the pleasure/interest screen at the 26-week weigh-in, and her sister Lorraine's Tennessee line. It also shows Ray eating chips. Other details imply more scenes: 'are you on?' hosts, the Columbus on-dose tests, dating-app on/off fields, musicians going off for the tour, and Army accession rules. Daily life has strong texture and many characters are implied.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicaid: 34 states plus DC cover generic semaglutide for obesity under CMS guidance, with the same continuation rule.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: it asserts that 34 states plus DC adopted obesity coverage within about two months of the Nov 2027 CMS guidance. State Medicaid obesity-drug coverage was patchy and retreating in 2026, and no budget, waiver or state-level chain explains the jump.

least_plausible_claims.quote: This fits the parent's 36–47% within-a-year restart rate and assumes better persistence (~45% at one year, up from 34–36%) because the drug now costs $49–69 cash or a few dollars' copay.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the persistence gain is assumed from price alone. The same world adds 90-day lapses, PDC ≥80% rules and 26-week weight cut-offs that push people off, and that contradicts it. The 30% cycling figure is tuned to fit rather than derived.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Pediatric: ~0.9% of under-18s, almost all aged 12–17 on label; under-12 use is still specialist-only and off-label.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: 0.9% of about 73M minors is roughly 650k children, or ~2.6% of all 12–17s. That is a very large jump from a 2026 baseline of ~0.6% of obese 8–11s, with no mechanism shown for teen uptake or for pediatric coverage.

rationale.badness: Mass access to effective drugs gives real health gains, and anhedonia is now measured, labelled (~4% vs 1.6%) and screened, so flourishing and epistemic scores are low. The harm is structural. Public coverage is conditioned on PDC≥80% and weigh-ins with 90-day lapses, and wellness surcharges are tied to BMI. Dose step-downs for pleasure risk coverage loss. The poorest, including non-expansion states and work-requirement disenrollees, are the heaviest and are left off the drug in a culture where being off it needs explaining. That drives autonomy and inequality up, though the world is a harder version of 2026 rather than a refuse-to-live-in society.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible in the fields and events. The 2027-06 settlement is the generic_collapse mechanism the envelope allows, the anhedonia label, conditioning, public expansion and normalisation are all traceable, the pipeline has only filings and CRLs, and no indications are added. mechanism: the settlement-to-generic chain and the Bridge-to-CMMI conversion are shown. Claims 1 and 2 are asserted rather than shown: the rapid 34-state Medicaid adoption, and the persistence gain that the conditioning rules would undercut. magnitude: on-drug 18.6 is inside 16.8–20.8 and ever-used 25 is inside 15–25.8, though near the upper edge. The income thirds average to 18.6 and bracket the national figure, and the age bands weight to ~18.5. The payer split sums to 100%, 20.5M ≈ 42% of 48.7M, and the $18.0B + $7.6B arithmetic checks. Minor flaws: the 0.9% pediatric figure (claim 3) and 'roughly flat (~$95B)' against a $76B baseline.
rationale.generativity: The Denise Ruelas scene is strong: the Tuesday injection, the adherence-app ping, 29 of 80 work hours, the 26-week weigh-in with the pleasure screen, and the nurse's warning that step-downs affect continuation. Her sister Lorraine, who is off it, and her husband Ray eating chips with the chip she holds imply further scenes. The world adds Columbus portion tests, 'are you on?' at table, dating-profile on/off fields, and sex therapists timing step-downs. Texture is dense and distinct.
